intro.data: One machine can’t get you all the way. Run the first machine, then feed its output straight into the second to reach the goal.
intro.alchemy: One apparatus can’t get you all the way. Run the first, then feed its output straight into the second to reach the goal.
intro.spellcraft: One rune can’t get you all the way. Cast the first, then feed its result straight into the second to reach the goal.
intro.abstract: One process can’t get you all the way. Apply the first, then feed its output straight into the second to reach the goal.

goal.data: Wire the start through both machines in order — A to B to C — ending at the goal.
goal.alchemy: Wire the start through both apparatuses in order — A to B to C — ending at the goal.
goal.spellcraft: Wire the start through both runes in order — A to B to C — ending at the goal.
goal.abstract: Wire the start through both processes in order — A to B to C — ending at the goal.

afterSuccess.data: You chained two machines into one longer transformation. Feeding the output of one process into another is called composition.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You chained two apparatuses into one longer transformation. Feeding the output of one process into another is called composition.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You chained two runes into one longer working. Feeding the result of one process into another is called composition.
afterSuccess.abstract: You chained two processes into one longer arrow. Feeding the output of one into another is called composition.

reveal.summary: When the target of one morphism matches the source of the next, you can compose them into a single arrow from the first source to the last target.
notation: g ∘ f means do f first, then g.
reveal.moreFormal: Given f : A → B and g : B → C, the composite g ∘ f : A → C is defined because target(f) = source(g) = B. Composition is read right-to-left, but applied first-to-last.
